correctness.rationale: Equal residues allow the joint mass on each ordered index pair to be written as A_ij(t) dt, since the first marginal for each index is dt. Symmetry gives symmetric matrices and uniformity unit row sums, so the long mass is the integral of twice the unordered long-edge weight; there is no extra factor of the fiber size. On n vertices, comparing the two parity degree sums gives minimum long mass at least n mod 2, met by short pairs and, on an odd fiber, a half-weight triangle. For the maximum, nonzero imbalance of one pair of opposite classes modulo four, when n is not divisible by four, forces at least unit unordered short-edge weight. The rest can use length-two four-block matchings, with a short pair, half-weight triangle, or half-weight pentagon supplying the initial exceptional block as appropriate. Thus (min,max) is (n mod 2,n - 2 times the indicator that n is not divisible by four). Independently solved both graph LPs for n=2 through 80 and checked the resulting rational primal and dual certificates exactly, including all constraints; replay with python3 /workspace/reproductions/5.py. The all-real-d statement follows analytically by weighting the two fiber sizes by d-r and r; for r=0 the larger fiber has no mass, and at d=1/2 the interval is {0}. Measurable piecewise-constant endpoint constructions preserve both marginals; mixing fills the interval. A graph-supported exchangeable law is involutive a.e.; successful edges in each fiber are transpositions, losing at least one vertex on an odd fiber even under imperfect support. Short pairs and a fixed unmatched vertex attain the bound. The existence statement for a deterministic exact-support coupling is existential, as given in the proof; even at d=1/4, for example, mixing the perfect short and long matchings gives a nondeterministic coupling. For d>1/2 the interval (1-d,d) of first coordinates cannot take either jump.
